final_candidates.decision_summary: Charge reversal in the antibody-accessible 375-386 loop likely disrupts m102.4-class contacts while preserving the ephrin-B2 binding interface.
Adjacent surface loop residue, exposed to antibody, adding arginine provides electrostatic/epitope perturbation without obvious receptor contact involvement.
Small threonine replaced with arginine alters the m102.4 epitope while major ephrin-binding interactions are retained, though the loop is near the receptor face.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence tools are available and current top-3 ranking is deemed adequate after self-review.

history.rationale: T303 is in an exposed surface loop of the G head that is likely contacted by m102.4-class antibodies; replacing it with a large charged arginine should create steric/electrostatic clash without removing an obvious conserved ephrin-binding contact.
Located near the m102.4 epitope but likely peripheral to the ephrin-binding groove; plausible to alter antibody recognition without abrogating receptor binding.
Small threonine replacement with arginine may alter the m102.4 epitope while preserving major ephrin-binding interactions. Moderate confidence because this loop is near the receptor-binding face.

K306 sits near a predicted neutralizing-antibody footprint on the receptor-binding lobe; charge reversal to glutamate can disrupt antibody affinity while avoiding conserved hydrophobic/aromatic contacts used for ephrin-B2 binding.
A charge swap in the same epitope region as T303, could disrupt antibody contacts while sparing key receptor interactions.
Charge inversion at a nearby loop residue can weaken antibody binding, but K306 may contribute to receptor interface contacts. Retain outside top three due a slightly higher preservation risk.

D376 is in a highly solvent-exposed loop region adjacent to the m102.4 epitope; an arginine substitution adds a bulky charged group that may block antibody binding with limited impact on the ephrin-B2 interface.
Known escape mutation that reduces m102.4 binding without affecting ephrin-B2/B3 binding; highest predicted tradeoff efficacy.

Charge reversal in the antibody-accessible 375-386 loop should disrupt m102.4-class contacts while this position is less likely to be a strict ephrin-B2 contact. Confidence slightly increased from self-review because this sidechain is solvent-oriented.

Q380 is located on a flexible antigenic loop near the G head surface and is less likely to be a core receptor contact; mutation to arginine introduces charge and size that can interfere with m102.4 epitope recognition.
Another escape site reported to retain receptor binding, compatible with antibody evasion and functional G protein.

Adjacent surface loop residue likely exposed to antibody; introducing arginine adds electrostatic/epitope perturbation without removing an obvious critical receptor contact. Retain as second-ranked candidate.

T513 is within a receptor-proximal loop but its side chain appears more directed toward antibody access than toward ephrin; a bulky arginine may disrupt m102.4 binding while preserving the key receptor contacts in this loop.
Position 513 lies in the ephrin-binding groove, so this mutation is likely to impair receptor binding despite potential antibody escape; deprioritized.
C-terminal proximity to receptor-binding elements raises preservation risk. Retain only as backup.
E304 is near the antibody-binding rim; charge reversal could weaken m102.4 contact. The mutation is included with lower confidence because this region partially overlaps receptor recognition.
Similar to T303 and K306, at the antibody interface but not a core receptor contact; moderate confidence.
Likely in the m102.4 footprint, but E304 may also participate in receptor binding, making this less safe than D376R or Q380R. Keep in active pool but not in final top three.
L456N creates a new N-linked glycosylation sequon in a surface-accessible segment, potentially masking part of the m102.4 epitope with a glycan shield while avoiding the main ephrin-binding cleft.
Potential glycosylation site may hinder antibody binding, but position is not well characterized; uncertain effect on receptor binding.
Potential loop perturbation without an established antibody or receptor contact role. Retain as a lower-confidence alternative.
G419N introduces a glycosylation sequon on an exposed loop, which could sterically block m102.4 recognition; the glycine replacement to asparagine is minimally disruptive to the protein core.
Possibly introduces a steric block to antibody, but no established role in ephrin binding; medium-low confidence.
Could add steric bulk to an exposed epitope region, but no strong evidence it selectively disrupts m102.4. Retain with low confidence.
Y511N creates an N-linked glycan on the receptor-binding loop, potentially hiding an m102.4 contact. Confidence is lower because Y511 may contribute to ephrin-B2 binding.
In the receptor-binding site, likely to reduce ephrin binding; low confidence for the required phenotype.
Aromatic sidechain loss could affect folding or receptor binding. Retain as a very low-confidence escape variant.
F426N adds a potential N-glycosylation site near a surface loop, which may impair antibody access; lower confidence due to uncertain surface exposure and possible structural effect.
May alter surface structure but not a known m102.4 contact; low confidence for immune escape.
Possible epitope contact but may destabilize the beta-propeller core. Low confidence.
